userdoc.notice: EIP-7702 delegate contract enforcing bitmasks, session keys, and velocity bounds.

devdoc.details: Enforcement model (defense in depth): 1. WHITELIST — preCheck reverts if call target not approved 2. PRE/POST BALANCE DELTA — snapshot before, enforce limit after 3. CUMULATIVE SPEND CAP — lifetime spend bounded at install postCheck runs INSIDE the userOp execution. Violation reverts atomically. Agent session key can sign ops, but cannot push funds past hook limits. Only smart account owner can change whitelist/limits — session key has no permission to touch firewall config.

preCheck(address,uint256,bytes).notice: Snapshots balance before execution and validates target.

userdoc.notice: Settled Protocol's on-chain firewall. ERC-7579 HOOK module (type 4).

devdoc.details: Enforcement model (defense in depth, all three must pass): 1. WHITELIST — preCheck reverts if the call target isn't an approved protocol contract (e.g. Aave Pool). 2. PRE/POST BALANCE DELTA — preCheck snapshots the account's tracked-asset balance; postCheck re-reads it and reverts if the drop exceeds the per-tx limit. 3. CUMULATIVE SPEND CAP — running total spend is capped over the account's lifetime allowance set at install time. Because postCheck runs INSIDE the same execution as the agent's call (ERC-4337 userOp), a violation reverts the entire operation atomically. The agent's session key can sign and submit ops, but it can never push funds past what this contract allows. Only the smart account itself (or its owner, configured at install time) can change its own whitelist/limits — the agent's session key has no permission to touch firewall config.

params.data: ABI-encoded (owner: address, trackedToken: address, maxSpendPerTx: uint256, maxSpendTotal: uint256, initialWhitelist: address[4]) initialWhitelist is fixed-size (max 4 targets) for v0.1 simplicity — e.g. [AavePool, AaveOracle/empty, empty, empty]. Use updateWhitelist() post-install to add more.

onInstall(bytes).notice: Called by the smart account during module installation.

onUninstall(bytes).notice: Wipes this account's config. Called by the account itself.

postCheck(bytes).notice: Decodes the snapshot and enforces atomic balance boundaries.

preCheck(address,uint256,bytes).notice: Snapshots the single tracked asset context before execution.

updateWhitelist(address,bool).notice: Only the account owner (not the agent's session key) may change which contracts the agent is allowed to call.

userdoc.notice: Settled Protocol's on-chain firewall. Installed as an ERC-7579 HOOK module (type 4) on every user's Biconomy Nexus smart account. One hook contract is shared by ALL Settled accounts — per-account config lives in this contract's storage, keyed by the smart account's address (`msg.sender` when the account calls in).

devdoc.details: Enforcement model (defense in depth): 1. WHITELIST — preCheck reverts if call target not approved 2. METHOD BLOCKLIST — blocks approve, increaseAllowance, transferFrom drains 3. PRE/POST BALANCE DELTA — snapshot before, enforce limit after 4. CUMULATIVE SPEND CAP — lifetime spend bounded at install 5. PAUSE — owner can emergency-stop all agent execution postCheck runs INSIDE the userOp execution. Violation reverts atomically. Agent session key can sign ops, but cannot push funds past hook limits. Only smart account owner can change whitelist/limits — session key has no permission to touch firewall config.

postCheck(bytes).details: If balance grew or held flat, nothing spent.

preCheck(address,uint256,bytes).details: Blocks: non-whitelisted targets, blocked selectors, paused accounts.

params.smartAccount: The address of the Smart Account to pause.

contracts/ACEGuard.vy.content:
# pragma version ^0.4.0
"""
@title ACEGuard Delegate
@notice EIP-7702 delegate contract enforcing bitmasks, session keys, and velocity bounds.
"""

# =============================================================
# Events
# =============================================================
event Executed:
    caller: indexed(address)
    target: indexed(address)
    value: uint256
    success: bool

event SessionKeySet:
    key: indexed(address)
    expires: uint256

event SessionKeyRevoked:
    key: indexed(address)

# =============================================================
# Structs & Storage
# =============================================================
struct EpochState:
    last_epoch: uint256
    calls: uint256
    value_spent: uint256

initialized: public(bool)
owner: public(address)

session_keys: public(HashMap[address, uint256])
epoch_states: public(HashMap[address, HashMap[address, EpochState]])

max_calls_per_epoch: public(uint256)
max_value_per_epoch: public(uint256)
epoch_duration: public(uint256)

allowed_targets: public(HashMap[address, bool])
is_allowed_selector: public(HashMap[bytes4, bool])

# =============================================================
# Initialization
# =============================================================
@external
def setup(
    _owner: address,
    _max_calls: uint256,
    _max_value: uint256,
    _epoch_duration: uint256
):
    assert not self.initialized, "Already initialized"
    assert _epoch_duration > 0, "Invalid duration"
    assert _owner != empty(address), "Invalid owner"

    self.owner = _owner
    self.initialized = True
    
    self.max_calls_per_epoch = _max_calls
    self.max_value_per_epoch = _max_value
    self.epoch_duration = _epoch_duration

# =============================================================
# Owner Configuration
# =============================================================
@external
def setSessionKey(key: address, duration: uint256):
    assert msg.sender == self.owner or msg.sender == self, "Not owner"

    new_expiration: uint256 = block.timestamp + duration
    self.session_keys[key] = new_expiration
    log SessionKeySet(key, new_expiration)

@external
def revokeSessionKey(key: address):
    assert msg.sender == self.owner or msg.sender == self, "Not owner"
    self.session_keys[key] = 0
    log SessionKeyRevoked(key)

@external
def setAllowedSelector(selector: bytes4, allowed: bool):
    assert msg.sender == self.owner or msg.sender == self, "Not owner"
    self.is_allowed_selector[selector] = allowed

@external
def setAllowedTarget(target: address, allowed: bool):
    assert msg.sender == self.owner or msg.sender == self, "Not owner"
    self.allowed_targets[target] = allowed

@external
def reset():
    assert msg.sender == self.owner or msg.sender == self, "Not owner"

    self.initialized = False
    self.owner = empty(address)

    self.max_calls_per_epoch = 0
    self.max_value_per_epoch = 0
    self.epoch_duration = 0


# =============================================================
# Execution
# =============================================================
@external
@payable
def execute(
    target: address,
    calldata: Bytes[1024]
) -> Bytes[1024]:
    caller: address = msg.sender
    
    # 1. Authorization check: Owner and self bypass session expiration
    if caller != self.owner and caller != self:
        expiry: uint256 = self.session_keys[caller]
        assert expiry > 0 and block.timestamp <= expiry, "Session invalid or expired"

    # 2. Selector check
    assert len(calldata) >= 4, "Calldata too short"
    target_selector: bytes4 = convert(slice(calldata, 0, 4), bytes4)
    assert self.is_allowed_selector[target_selector], "Unauthorized Selector"

    # 3. Target check 
    assert self.allowed_targets[target], "Target not allowed"

    # 4. Epoch velocity limits
    current_epoch: uint256 = block.timestamp // self.epoch_duration
    state: EpochState = self.epoch_states[caller][target]

    if state.last_epoch != current_epoch:
        state.calls = 0
        state.value_spent = 0
        state.last_epoch = current_epoch

    assert state.calls < self.max_calls_per_epoch, "ACE: Call limit"
    assert state.value_spent + msg.value <= self.max_value_per_epoch, "ACE: Value limit"

    state.calls += 1
    state.value_spent += msg.value

    # Commit memory struct back to storage mapping
    self.epoch_states[caller][target] = state

    # 5. Raw execution call
    response: Bytes[1024] = raw_call(
        target,
        calldata,
        max_outsize=1024,
        value=msg.value,
        revert_on_failure=True
    )

    log Executed(caller, target, msg.value, True)
    return response

@external
@payable
def __default__():
    pass

contracts/Executioner.vy.content:
# @version 0.4.3
"""
@title FirewallHook
@notice Settled Protocol's on-chain firewall. ERC-7579 HOOK module (type 4).

@dev Enforcement model (defense in depth):
    1. WHITELIST — preCheck reverts if call target not approved
    2. PRE/POST BALANCE DELTA — snapshot before, enforce limit after
    3. CUMULATIVE SPEND CAP — lifetime spend bounded at install

    postCheck runs INSIDE the userOp execution. Violation reverts atomically.
    Agent session key can sign ops, but cannot push funds past hook limits.
    Only smart account owner can change whitelist/limits — session key has
    no permission to touch firewall config.
"""


interface IERC20:
    def balanceOf(account: address) -> uint256: view

HOOK_MODULE_TYPE: constant(uint256) = 4

struct AccountConfig:
    initialized: bool
    paused: bool
    owner: address
    trackedToken: address
    maxSpendPerTx: uint256
    maxSpendTotal: uint256
    spentTotal: uint256

configs: public(HashMap[address, AccountConfig])
whitelist: public(HashMap[address, HashMap[address, bool]])
approvedAllowances: public(HashMap[address, HashMap[address, HashMap[address, uint256]]])


event HookInstalled:
    account: indexed(address)
    owner: address
    maxSpendPerTx: uint256
    maxSpendTotal: uint256

event WhitelistUpdated:
    account: indexed(address)
    target: indexed(address)
    allowed: bool

event SpendRecorded:
    account: indexed(address)
    amount: uint256
    newTotal: uint256

event Violation:
    account: indexed(address)
    reason: String[64]

@external
@view
def isModuleType(typeID: uint256) -> bool:
    return typeID == HOOK_MODULE_TYPE

@external
@view
def isInitialized(smartAccount: address) -> bool:
    return self.configs[smartAccount].initialized

@external
def onInstall(data: Bytes[1024]):
    account: address = msg.sender
    assert not self.configs[account].initialized, "already installed"

    owner: address = empty(address)
    trackedToken: address = empty(address)
    maxSpendPerTx: uint256 = 0
    maxSpendTotal: uint256 = 0
    initialWhitelist: address[4] = empty(address[4])

    owner, trackedToken, maxSpendPerTx, maxSpendTotal, initialWhitelist = abi_decode(
        data, (address, address, uint256, uint256, address[4])
    )

    assert owner != empty(address), "owner required"
    assert maxSpendPerTx > 0 and maxSpendPerTx <= maxSpendTotal, "bad limits"

    self.configs[account] = AccountConfig(
        initialized=True,
        paused=False,
        owner=owner,
        trackedToken=trackedToken,
        maxSpendPerTx=maxSpendPerTx,
        maxSpendTotal=maxSpendTotal,
        spentTotal=0,
    )

    for target: address in initialWhitelist:
        if target != empty(address):
            self.whitelist[account][target] = True
            log WhitelistUpdated(account=account, target=target, allowed=True)

    log HookInstalled(
        account=account,
        owner=owner,
        maxSpendPerTx=maxSpendPerTx,
        maxSpendTotal=maxSpendTotal,
    )

@external
def onUninstall(data: Bytes[1024]):
    account: address = msg.sender
    self.configs[account] = empty(AccountConfig)

@external
def updateWhitelist(target: address, allowed: bool):
    account: address = msg.sender
    cfg: AccountConfig = self.configs[account]
    assert cfg.initialized, "not installed"
    assert msg.sender == cfg.owner, "only owner can update whitelist"
    self.whitelist[account][target] = allowed
    log WhitelistUpdated(account=account, target=target, allowed=allowed)

@external
def updateLimits(maxSpendPerTx: uint256, maxSpendTotal: uint256):
    account: address = msg.sender
    cfg: AccountConfig = self.configs[account]
    assert msg.sender == cfg.owner, "only owner can update limits"
    assert cfg.initialized, "not installed"
    assert maxSpendPerTx > 0 and maxSpendPerTx <= maxSpendTotal, "bad limits"
    assert maxSpendTotal >= cfg.spentTotal, "below already-spent total"

    self.configs[account].maxSpendPerTx = maxSpendPerTx
    self.configs[account].maxSpendTotal = maxSpendTotal

@internal
@view
def _balanceOf(account: address, token: address) -> uint256:
    if token == empty(address):
        return account.balance
    return staticcall IERC20(token).balanceOf(account)

@internal
@pure
def _decodeTarget(msgData: Bytes[8192]) -> address:
    """
    Extract target from ERC-7579 single execution msg.data.
    Layout: selector(4) + mode(32) + offset(32) + length(32) + target(20) + ...
    """
    assert len(msgData) >= 68, "malformed calldata"

    callType: Bytes[1] = slice(msgData, 4, 1)
    assert convert(callType, uint256) == 0, "only single-call execution allowed"

    offsetBytes: Bytes[32] = slice(msgData, 36, 32)
    offset: uint256 = convert(offsetBytes, uint256)
    dataStart: uint256 = 4 + offset

    assert len(msgData) >= dataStart + 52, "malformed execution calldata"

    # target is at dataStart + 32 (after the length word)
    targetBytes: Bytes[20] = slice(msgData, dataStart + 32, 20)
    return convert(targetBytes, address)

@external
def preCheck(msgSender: address, msgValue: uint256, msgData: Bytes[8192]) -> Bytes[2048]:
    """
    @notice Snapshots balance before execution and validates target.
    """
    account: address = msg.sender
    cfg: AccountConfig = self.configs[account]
    
    assert cfg.initialized, "firewall not installed"

    # Extract and validate target
    target: address = self._decodeTarget(msgData)
    assert self.whitelist[account][target], "target not whitelisted"

    # Snapshot balance
    balanceBefore: uint256 = self._balanceOf(account, cfg.trackedToken)

    # Return hook data for postCheck
    return abi_encode(account, balanceBefore)

@external
def postCheck(hookData: Bytes[2048]):
    """
    @notice Enforces spend limits after execution.
    """
    account: address = empty(address)
    balanceBefore: uint256 = 0
    
    account, balanceBefore = abi_decode(hookData, (address, uint256))
    assert account == msg.sender, "hookData/account mismatch"

    cfg: AccountConfig = self.configs[account]
    balanceAfter: uint256 = self._balanceOf(account, cfg.trackedToken)

    # If balance grew or held flat, nothing spent
    if balanceAfter >= balanceBefore:
        return

    # Calculate spend and enforce limits
    spent: uint256 = balanceBefore - balanceAfter
    assert spent <= cfg.maxSpendPerTx, "exceeds per-tx spending limit"
    assert cfg.spentTotal + spent <= cfg.maxSpendTotal, "exceeds total spending limit"

    self.configs[account].spentTotal += spent
    log SpendRecorded(account=account, amount=spent, newTotal=self.configs[account].spentTotal)

@external
@view
def getConfig(account: address) -> AccountConfig:
    return self.configs[account]

contracts/FirewallHook.vy.content:
# @version 0.4.3
"""
@title FirewallHook
@notice Settled Protocol's on-chain firewall. Installed as an ERC-7579 HOOK
        module (type 4) on every user's Biconomy Nexus smart account.

        One hook contract is shared by ALL Settled accounts — per-account
        config lives in this contract's storage, keyed by the smart
        account's address (`msg.sender` when the account calls in).

@dev    Enforcement model (defense in depth, all three must pass):
        1. WHITELIST  — preCheck reverts if the call target isn't an
                         approved protocol contract (e.g. Aave Pool).
        2. PRE/POST BALANCE DELTA — preCheck snapshots the account's
                         tracked-asset balance; postCheck re-reads it and
                         reverts if the drop exceeds the per-tx limit.
        3. CUMULATIVE SPEND CAP — running total spend is capped over the
                         account's lifetime allowance set at install time.

        Because postCheck runs INSIDE the same execution as the agent's
        call (ERC-4337 userOp), a violation reverts the entire operation
        atomically. The agent's session key can sign and submit ops, but
        it can never push funds past what this contract allows.

        Only the smart account itself (or its owner, configured at
        install time) can change its own whitelist/limits — the agent's
        session key has no permission to touch firewall config.
"""

# ── Interfaces ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface IERC20:
    def balanceOf(account: address) -> uint256: view

interface IdentityRegistry:
    def isVerified(user: address) -> bool: view

interface IComplianceProvider:
    def isCompliant(agent: address, rwa_token: address, action_type: uint256) -> bool: view

# ── Module type constant (ERC-7579) ────────────────────────────────────
HOOK_MODULE_TYPE: constant(uint256) = 4

# ── Storage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct AccountConfig:
    initialized: bool
    paused: bool
    owner: address          # EOA/Privy embedded wallet that controls config
    trackedToken: address   # token whose balance we protect; empty(address) = native
    maxSpendPerTx: uint256  # hard cap on balance drop in a single user op
    maxSpendTotal: uint256  # lifetime cap (resets only by owner action)
    spentTotal: uint256     # cumulative spend consumed so far

# account => config
configs: public(HashMap[address, AccountConfig])

# account => target contract => allowed to call
whitelist: public(HashMap[address, HashMap[address, bool]])

# account => count of violations that were caught and reverted
# (incremented via a separate non-reverting recorder pattern — see note
#  on `recordViolation` below)
violationCount: public(HashMap[address, uint256])

# Pseudocode for where Settled is heading
identityRegistry: public(address)  # Settled's OWNERID contract



# ── Events ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

event HookInstalled:
    account: indexed(address)
    owner: address
    maxSpendPerTx: uint256
    maxSpendTotal: uint256

event WhitelistUpdated:
    account: indexed(address)
    target: indexed(address)
    allowed: bool

event SpendRecorded:
    account: indexed(address)
    amount: uint256
    newTotal: uint256

event LimitsUpdated:
    account: indexed(address)
    maxSpendPerTx: uint256
    maxSpendTotal: uint256

event Violation:
    account: indexed(address)
    reason: String[64]

event EmergencyPaused:
    account: indexed(address)
    paused: bool



# ── ERC-7579 module identity ───────────────────────────────────────────

@external
@view
def isModuleType(typeID: uint256) -> bool:
    return typeID == HOOK_MODULE_TYPE


@external
@view
def isInitialized(smartAccount: address) -> bool:
    return self.configs[smartAccount].initialized


# ── Install / uninstall ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

@external
def onInstall(data: Bytes[1024]):
    """
    @notice Called by the smart account during module installation.
    @param data ABI-encoded (owner: address, trackedToken: address,
                 maxSpendPerTx: uint256, maxSpendTotal: uint256,
                 initialWhitelist: address[4])
            initialWhitelist is fixed-size (max 4 targets) for v0.1
            simplicity — e.g. [AavePool, AaveOracle/empty, empty, empty].
            Use updateWhitelist() post-install to add more.
    """
    account: address = msg.sender
    assert not self.configs[account].initialized, "already installed"

    owner: address = empty(address)
    trackedToken: address = empty(address)
    maxSpendPerTx: uint256 = 0
    maxSpendTotal: uint256 = 0
    initialWhitelist: address[4] = empty(address[4])

    owner, trackedToken, maxSpendPerTx, maxSpendTotal, initialWhitelist = abi_decode(
        data, (address, address, uint256, uint256, address[4])
    )

    assert owner != empty(address), "owner required"
    assert maxSpendPerTx > 0 and maxSpendPerTx <= maxSpendTotal, "bad limits"

    self.configs[account] = AccountConfig(
        initialized=True,
        paused=False,
        owner=owner,
        trackedToken=trackedToken,
        maxSpendPerTx=maxSpendPerTx,
        maxSpendTotal=maxSpendTotal,
        spentTotal=0,
    )

    for target: address in initialWhitelist:
        if target != empty(address):
            self.whitelist[account][target] = True
            log WhitelistUpdated(account=account, target=target, allowed=True)

    log HookInstalled(
        account=account,
        owner=owner,
        maxSpendPerTx=maxSpendPerTx,
        maxSpendTotal=maxSpendTotal,
    )


@external
def onUninstall(data: Bytes[1024]):
    """@notice Wipes this account's config. Called by the account itself."""
    account: address = msg.sender
    self.configs[account] = empty(AccountConfig)
    # Note: whitelist entries are left as dead storage (cheaper than
    # iterating to clear); they're inert once `initialized` is False
    # since preCheck/postCheck both gate on initialized.


# ── Owner-controlled config updates (NOT callable by the agent) ────────

@external
def updateWhitelist(target: address, allowed: bool):
    """@notice Only the account owner (not the agent's session key) may
               change which contracts the agent is allowed to call."""
    account: address = msg.sender
    cfg: AccountConfig = self.configs[account]
    assert cfg.initialized, "not installed"
    # NOTE: this function is called BY the smart account on behalf of the
    # owner — the account's own validator module already enforces that
    # only the owner's signature (not the session key) can trigger calls
    # to this function, since it's not in the session key's permitted
    # target list configured at session-key creation time.
    self.whitelist[account][target] = allowed
    log WhitelistUpdated(account=account, target=target, allowed=allowed)


@external
def updateLimits(maxSpendPerTx: uint256, maxSpendTotal: uint256):
    account: address = msg.sender
    cfg: AccountConfig = self.configs[account]
    assert cfg.initialized, "not installed"
    assert maxSpendPerTx > 0 and maxSpendPerTx <= maxSpendTotal, "bad limits"
    assert maxSpendTotal >= cfg.spentTotal, "below already-spent total"

    self.configs[account].maxSpendPerTx = maxSpendPerTx
    self.configs[account].maxSpendTotal = maxSpendTotal
    log LimitsUpdated(account=account, maxSpendPerTx=maxSpendPerTx, maxSpendTotal=maxSpendTotal)


# ── Internal: read the tracked asset's balance for an account ──────────

@internal
@view
def _balanceOf(account: address, token: address) -> uint256:
    if token == empty(address):
        return account.balance
    return staticcall IERC20(token).balanceOf(account)

@internal
@view
def _getBalance(account: address, token: address) -> uint256:
    if token == empty(address):
        return account.balance
        
    return staticcall IERC20(token).balanceOf(account)

@internal
def _verifyIdentity(account: address):
    assert staticcall IdentityRegistry(self.identityRegistry).isVerified(
        self.configs[account].owner
    ), "owner identity not attested"

# ── Internal: pull (target, value) out of the execution calldata ───────

@internal
@pure
def _decodeTarget(msgData: Bytes[8192]) -> address:
    """
    @dev Verified against Nexus's actual HookManager: preCheck receives
         the FULL `msg.data` of the call to `execute()` /
         `executeFromExecutor()` — selector included, not an unwrapped
         payload. Layout:

           [0:4]    function selector
           [4:36]   ExecutionMode (32 bytes packed struct);
                    byte 0 of this word = CallType
                    (0x00 = single, 0x01 = batch, 0xFF = delegatecall)
           [36:68]  ABI offset (relative to byte 4) to the
                    `executionCalldata` bytes parameter
           at (4 + offset):
             [0:32]   length of executionCalldata
             [32:52]  target address (20 bytes — for CALLTYPE_SINGLE the
                      layout is target(20) ++ value(32) ++ callData)
             [52:84]  value
             [84:]    callData

    @dev v0.1 SECURITY DECISION: only CALLTYPE_SINGLE is accepted.
         Batched executions are rejected outright — per-call whitelist
         and spend-delta checks don't compose safely across an
         arbitrary batch (e.g. a batch could combine a whitelisted call
         with a hidden second call), and v0.1's templates only ever
         need to make one call per agent step anyway.
    """
    assert len(msgData) >= 68, "malformed calldata"

    callType: Bytes[1] = slice(msgData, 4, 1)
    assert convert(callType, uint256) == 0, "only single-call execution allowed"

    offsetBytes: Bytes[32] = slice(msgData, 36, 32)
    offset: uint256 = convert(offsetBytes, uint256)
    dataStart: uint256 = 4 + offset

    assert len(msgData) >= dataStart + 52, "malformed execution calldata"

    targetBytes: Bytes[20] = slice(msgData, dataStart + 32, 20)
    return convert(targetBytes, address)

# # ── Improved Target Extraction ──────────────────────────────────────────
@internal
@pure
def _extractTargets(msgData: Bytes[8192]) -> DynArray[address, 16]:
    """
    Robust target extraction for Biconomy Nexus (ERC-7579)
    Works with both single calls and batches from Privy + Biconomy backend.
    """
    targets: DynArray[address, 16] = []
    
    if len(msgData) < 36:  # selector (4) + mode (32)
        return targets

    # Extract ExecutionMode (bytes32 after selector)
    mode: bytes32 = convert(slice(msgData, 4, 32), bytes32)
    
    # Call type is the first byte of the mode
    callType: uint8 = convert(slice(mode, 0, 1), uint8)

    if callType == 0:  # Single Call
        # Layout: target (address) + value (uint256) + callData (bytes)
        if len(msgData) >= 4 + 32 + 32 + 20:   # selector + mode + offset? + target
            # Standard single call target position
            target: address = convert(slice(msgData, 68, 20), address)
            if target != empty(address):
                targets.append(target)

    elif callType == 1:  # Batch Call (most common for agents)
        # executionCalldata starts with offset to Execution[] array
        if len(msgData) < 4 + 32 + 32:
            return targets
            
        arrayOffset: uint256 = convert(slice(msgData, 36, 32), uint256)  # offset after mode
        dataStart: uint256 = 4 + arrayOffset
        
        if len(msgData) < dataStart + 32:
            return targets
            
        arrayLen: uint256 = convert(slice(msgData, dataStart, 32), uint256)
        
        # Each Execution struct = 32 (target padded) + 32 (value) + 32 (calldata offset) = 96 bytes
        for i: uint256 in range(16):
            if i >= arrayLen:
                break
                
            execStart: uint256 = dataStart + 32 + (i * 96)
            if len(msgData) >= execStart + 32:
                target: address = convert(slice(msgData, execStart, 20), address)
                if target != empty(address):
                    targets.append(target)

    return targets

@external
def preCheck(msgSender: address, msgValue: uint256, msgData: Bytes[8192]) -> Bytes[2048]:
    """
    @notice Snapshots the single tracked asset context before execution.
    """
    account: address = msg.sender
    cfg: AccountConfig = self.configs[account]
    
    assert cfg.initialized, "firewall not installed"

    # Robust target extraction from your existing code
    target: address = self._decodeTarget(msgData)
    assert self.whitelist[account][target], "target not whitelisted"

    # Single, clean balance snapshot handed directly to memory stack
    balanceBefore: uint256 = self._getBalance(account, cfg.trackedToken)

    # Hand back as a clean tuple payload matching postCheck expectations
    return abi_encode(account, balanceBefore)


@external
def postCheck(hookData: Bytes[2048]):
    """
    @notice Decodes the snapshot and enforces atomic balance boundaries.
    """
    account: address = empty(address)
    balanceBefore: uint256 = 0
    
    # PERFECT ALIGNMENT: Decodes the clean tuple schema flawlessly
    account, balanceBefore = abi_decode(hookData, (address, uint256))
    assert account == msg.sender, "hookData/account mismatch"

    cfg: AccountConfig = self.configs[account]
    balanceAfter: uint256 = self._getBalance(account, cfg.trackedToken)

    # If balance grew or held flat (e.g. profitable rebalance or compound), exit safely
    if balanceAfter >= balanceBefore:
        return

    # If capital dropped, ensure it did not breach the firewall boundaries
    spent: uint256 = balanceBefore - balanceAfter
    assert spent <= cfg.maxSpendPerTx, "exceeds per-tx spending limit"
    assert cfg.spentTotal + spent <= cfg.maxSpendTotal, "exceeds total spending limit"

    self.configs[account].spentTotal += spent
    log SpendRecorded(account=account, amount=spent, newTotal=self.configs[account].spentTotal)

"""

"""

interface IERC20:

    def transfer(_to: address, _value: uint256) -> bool: nonpayable
    def balanceOf(_owner: address) -> uint256: view

@deploy

    RWA = _rwa
    USDC = _usdc

@external
def swap(tokenIn: address, tokenOut: address, amount: uint256):
    """
    @notice 1:1 swap for testing
    @dev Pulls tokenIn from caller, sends tokenOut to caller
    """
    assert (tokenIn == RWA and tokenOut == USDC) or (tokenIn == USDC and tokenOut == RWA), "Invalid pair"
    assert tokenIn != tokenOut, "Same token"
    
    # Pull tokenIn from caller (proxy)
    success: bool = extcall IERC20(tokenIn).transferFrom(msg.sender, self, amount)
    assert success, "Transfer in failed"
    
    # Determine amount out (1:1, adjust for decimals)
    amountOut: uint256 = amount
    if tokenIn == RWA and tokenOut == USDC:
        amountOut = amount * 10**6 // 10**18  # RWA 18dec → USDC 6dec
    elif tokenIn == USDC and tokenOut == RWA:
        amountOut = amount * 10**18 // 10**6  # USDC 6dec → RWA 18dec
    
    # Send tokenOut to caller (proxy)
    success = extcall IERC20(tokenOut).transfer(msg.sender, amountOut)
    assert success, "Transfer out failed"

    self.totalSupply += amount

contracts/Proxy.vy.content:
# pragma version ^0.4.0
"""
@title SettledDeltaProxy
@notice Secure ERC-8232 agency proxy with strict delta enforcement
"""

interface IERC20:
    def balanceOf(_owner: address) -> uint256: view

interface IComplianceProvider:
    def isCompliant(agent: address, rwa_token: address, action_type: uint256) -> bool: view

struct Permission:
    bitmask: uint256
    expiry: uint256

permissions: public(HashMap[bytes32, Permission])
bit_to_selector: public(HashMap[uint256, bytes4])

owner: public(address)
is_initialized: bool
identity_registry: public(address)
compliance_provider: public(address)
USDC: public(address)
MIN_USDC_PER_RWA: public(uint256)  # e.g., 0.95e6 = $0.95 per RWA

# Pricing or Oracle validation mechanism should be plugged here to prevent 1-wei bypasses.
# For strict delta validation, we track required exchange rates or min returns.

@internal
@view
def _get_permission_key(agent: address, rwa_token: address) -> bytes32:
    return keccak256(abi_encode(agent, rwa_token))

@external
def initialize(_owner: address, _identity_registry: address, _compliance: address, _usdc: address):
    assert not self.is_initialized, "Already initialized"
    self.owner = _owner
    self.identity_registry = _identity_registry
    self.compliance_provider = _compliance
    self.USDC = _usdc
    self.is_initialized = True
    # Represent $0.95 in USDC's smallest units (6 decimals): 0.95 * 1e6 = 950000
    self.MIN_USDC_PER_RWA = 0  # $0.95 (6 decimals) per RWA

@external
def mapSelector(bit: uint256, selector: bytes4):
    assert msg.sender == self.owner, "NOT_OWNER"
    self.bit_to_selector[bit] = selector

@external
def setAgentPermission(agent: address, rwa_token: address, bitmask: uint256, expiry: uint256):
    assert msg.sender == self.owner, "NOT_OWNER"
    key: bytes32 = self._get_permission_key(agent, rwa_token)
    self.permissions[key] = Permission(bitmask=bitmask, expiry=expiry)

# @internal
# def _enforce_delta(usdc_0: uint256, rwa_0: uint256, usdc_1: uint256, rwa_1: uint256):
#     if rwa_1 < rwa_0:
#         # Prevent 1-wei entry exploitation: Check that incoming USDC is non-zero
#         # Optimally, include a slippage or price calculation here.
#         assert usdc_1 > usdc_0, "Settled: RWA drained without USDC intake"


@internal
def _enforce_delta(usdc_0: uint256, rwa_0: uint256, usdc_1: uint256, rwa_1: uint256):
    if rwa_1 < rwa_0:
        rwa_sold: uint256 = rwa_0 - rwa_1
        usdc_gained: uint256 = usdc_1 - usdc_0
        
        # Minimum price: at least MIN_USDC_PER_RWA per RWA sold
        # rwa_sold has 18 decimals, MIN_USDC_PER_RWA has 6 decimals; divide by 10**18 to normalize
        min_usdc: uint256 = rwa_sold * self.MIN_USDC_PER_RWA // 10 ** 18
        assert usdc_gained >= min_usdc, "Settled: Price below floor"
@external
@nonreentrant
def performAgencyAction(
    rwa_token: address,
    action_type_bit: uint256,
    call_data: Bytes[1024]
) -> Bytes[1024]:
    key: bytes32 = self._get_permission_key(msg.sender, rwa_token)
    perm: Permission = self.permissions[key]
    
    assert block.timestamp <= perm.expiry, "AGENCY_EXPIRED"
    
    # Vyper 0.4.x: use << operator
    shift_mask: uint256 = 1 << action_type_bit
    assert (perm.bitmask & shift_mask) > 0, "PERMISSION_DENIED"
    
    actual_selector: bytes4 = convert(slice(call_data, 0, 4), bytes4)
    expected_selector: bytes4 = self.bit_to_selector[action_type_bit]
    assert actual_selector == expected_selector, "SELECTOR_MISMATCH"
    
    usdc_0: uint256 = 0
    rwa_0: uint256 = 0
    
    if rwa_token != empty(address):
        usdc_0 = staticcall IERC20(self.USDC).balanceOf(self)
        rwa_0 = staticcall IERC20(rwa_token).balanceOf(self)
    
    response: Bytes[1024] = raw_call(rwa_token, call_data, max_outsize=1024, revert_on_failure=True)
    
    if rwa_token != empty(address):
        usdc_1: uint256 = staticcall IERC20(self.USDC).balanceOf(self)
        rwa_1: uint256 = staticcall IERC20(rwa_token).balanceOf(self)
        self._enforce_delta(usdc_0, rwa_0, usdc_1, rwa_1)
    
    return response

@external
@nonreentrant
def executeTX(_target: address, _value: uint256, _data: Bytes[4096], _tracked_rwa: address) -> Bytes[4096]:
    """
    @notice Direct execution path limited strictly to the owner with atomic delta tracking.
    """
    assert msg.sender == self.owner, "NOT_OWNER"
    
    usdc_0: uint256 = staticcall IERC20(self.USDC).balanceOf(self)
    rwa_0: uint256 = 0
    if _tracked_rwa != empty(address):
        rwa_0 = staticcall IERC20(_tracked_rwa).balanceOf(self)
        
    response: Bytes[4096] = raw_call(_target, _data, value=_value, max_outsize=4096, revert_on_failure=True)
    
    if _tracked_rwa != empty(address):
        usdc_1: uint256 = staticcall IERC20(self.USDC).balanceOf(self)
        rwa_1: uint256 = staticcall IERC20(_tracked_rwa).balanceOf(self)
        self._enforce_delta(usdc_0, rwa_0, usdc_1, rwa_1)
        
    return response

# @version ^0.4.0

from ethereum.ercs import IERC20


struct Session:
    approved: bool
    max_amount: uint256      # Max this spender can spend from vault
    spent: uint256           # How much they've spent
    expires: uint256         # Timestamp

event SessionCreated:
    spender: indexed(address)
    amount: indexed(uint256)
    duration: indexed(uint256)

event Withdrawal:
    sender: indexed(address)
    destination: indexed(address)
    amount: indexed(uint256)

event SessionTerminated:
    _for: indexed(address)


sessions: public(HashMap[address, Session])
usdc: public(address)
owner: public(address)


@deploy
def __init__(_usdc: address):
    self.usdc = _usdc
    self.owner = msg.sender


@external
def balanceOfSession() -> uint256:
    return self.sessions[msg.sender].max_amount - self.sessions[msg.sender].spent

@external
def close_session():
    """Buyer can revoke anytime"""
    self.sessions[msg.sender].approved = False
    log SessionTerminated(msg.sender)

@external
@nonreentrant
def create_session(max_amount: uint256, duration_days: uint256):
    """
    Create/extend a session for msg.sender (the relayer).
    This authorizes them to spend up to max_amount from SnowGate vault.
    """
    # Only owner or admin can create sessions? Or anyone can self-authorize?
    # For now: anyone can create their own session (they're authorizing themselves to spend vault funds)
    # But actually, this should probably be restricted to approved relayers
    
    new_max: uint256 = max_amount
    new_spent: uint256 = 0
    
    # If extending existing session, preserve spent amount unless resetting
    current: Session = self.sessions[msg.sender]
    if current.approved and current.expires > block.timestamp:
        # Extending - keep spent amount, add new budget to remaining
        remaining: uint256 = current.max_amount - current.spent
        new_max = remaining + max_amount  # Add new budget to remaining
        new_spent = current.spent
    
    self.sessions[msg.sender] = Session({
        approved: True,
        max_amount: new_max,
        spent: new_spent,
        expires: block.timestamp + (duration_days * 86400)
    })
    
    log SessionCreated(msg.sender, new_max, duration_days)
